segments.t: At the ASK offices, Camille is terrified by the impressive resumes of outside applicants for the junior agent post. Her friends Noémie and Hervé spot a top contender and consider dirty tricks to help Camille. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Attends, viens là, Camille.
Imiter Hicham à ton entretien? Tu ne devrais pas être toi-même?
J'ai la tête qui tourne.
Les CV des candidats, c'est du niveau Harvard!
Tu as l'avantage de travailler ici.
Regarde, c'est Eugénie Léon-Brun.
Droit, spécialisée en propriété intellectuelle.
Trois ans en production, puis deux chez VMA.
Et en plus elle est mignonne, Hicham va adorer.
Je peux la déstabiliser si tu veux.
Tu ne peux pas faire ça, ça ne se fait pas!
Oui, ce serait ignoble. Quand même...
Allez, Noémie, démolis la rivale!
Je vais lui parler de la PNL et du langage corporel.
Tu as vraiment fait une formation?
C'est comme ça que j'ai appris à contrôler mes émotions.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Attends, viens là, Camille.
'Wait, come over here, Camille.' Hervé calls Camille over to discuss her interview. The key word here means 'wait', paired with 'here' to make the point clear.
Imiter Hicham à ton entretien? Tu ne devrais pas être toi-même?
'Imitate Hicham at your interview? Shouldn't you be yourself?' Hervé questions the psychological tactic. Hervé pairs the verb meaning 'to imitate' with the noun for 'interview'.
J'ai la tête qui tourne.
'My head is spinning.' Camille confesses her mounting panic. Listen for the expression meaning 'I have', which leads naturally into 'spins'.
Les CV des candidats, c'est du niveau Harvard!
'The candidates' resumes are Harvard level!' Camille marvels at the fierce competition. Listen for the expression meaning 'resumes', which leads naturally into 'level'.
Tu as l'avantage de travailler ici.
'You have the advantage of working here.' Noémie reminds Camille of her insider status. Noémie opens with the word for 'have' and lands on 'here' at the close.
Regarde, c'est Eugénie Léon-Brun.
'Look, that is Eugenie Leon-Brun.' Noémie identifies the most formidable rival. Noémie gives a direct command form using the verb for 'look'.
Droit, spécialisée en propriété intellectuelle.

'Law school, specialized in intellectual property.' Noémie recites Eugenie's stellar academic qualifications. The adjective meaning 'intellectual' agrees in gender and number with masculine noun 'law'.
Trois ans en production, puis deux chez VMA.
'Three years in production, then two at VMA.' Noémie details Eugenie's extensive industry experience. Listen for the expression meaning 'three', which leads naturally into 'two'.
Et en plus elle est mignonne, Hicham va adorer.
'And plus she is pretty, Hicham is going to love her.' Noémie points out Eugenie's obvious appeal. The adverb meaning 'addition' sharpens the verb for 'is' here.
Je peux la déstabiliser si tu veux.
'I can destabilize her if you want.' Noémie offers to take matters into her own hands. The verb meaning 'can' anchors the whole remark.
Tu ne peux pas faire ça, ça ne se fait pas!
'You cannot do that, it is not done!' Camille refuses to win through dirty tricks. The impersonal expression 'that' denotes socially unacceptable behavior.
Oui, ce serait ignoble. Quand même...
'Yes, that would be disgraceful. Still...' Noémie wavers between professional ethics and agency loyalty. The verb meaning 'would be' anchors the whole remark.
Allez, Noémie, démolis la rivale!
'Go on, Noémie, crush the rival!' Hervé enthusiastically encourages the sabotage. Hervé opens with the word for 'go on' and lands on 'rival' at the close.
Je vais lui parler de la PNL et du langage corporel.
'I will talk to her about NLP and body language.' Noémie devises a psychological scheme. The near future 'I' indicates imminent action.
Tu as vraiment fait une formation?
'Did you really take a training course?' Camille asks skeptically about Noémie's qualifications. Notice how the verb for 'have' leads straight into 'training course'.
C'est comme ça que j'ai appris à contrôler mes émotions.

'That is how I learned to control my emotions.' Noémie claims newfound emotional mastery. The key word here means 'I have', paired with 'emotions' to make the point clear. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

Facing stiff outside competition for the junior agent post, Camille feels inadequate next to Eugenie's credentials. Despite Camille's moral objections, Noémie sets out to sabotage the applicant's interview. See you next time!
À demain!
